special_flags: Vitamin C (High Dose) + Glutathione in same bag (allowed)

preflight_checks: Confirm patient name + DOB (or clinic ID).
Confirm consent for IV session and selected option.
Baseline vitals required: BP, HR, SpO2, Temp; record baseline values before starting infusion.
Baseline symptom check required: dizziness (yes/no), nausea (yes/no), anxiety/palpitations (yes/no), headache (yes/no).
Hard stop screen: confirm NO chest pain now, NO shortness of breath now, NO fainting episode today, NO confusion or severe weakness now; if any present, do not proceed and call clinician.

Review key safety items: pregnancy/breastfeeding status, kidney disease, G6PD status, severe allergy/anaphylaxis history, asthma/reactive airway history, seizure history; if any are Yes/Unsure or unclear, escalate to clinician before proceeding.
Verify today’s vitals are acceptable for infusion: SpO2 98% and BP 100/70 documented; confirm patient feels well to proceed.
setup_steps: Gather equipment: IV cannula (20–24G), tourniquet, antiseptic prep, sterile gauze, transparent dressing, tape, extension line, saline flush syringes, sharps container, IV administration set, IV stand, labels/marker, gloves; ensure emergency supplies are available per clinic policy.
Prepare Bag 1: 250 ml Normal Saline (0.9%); label with patient identifiers, date/time, and additives.
Add ingredients to Bag 1: Vitamin C (High Dose) 2000 mg and Glutathione 1200 mg; mix gently and confirm clarity/compatibility.
Note admin guidance: Vitamin C + Glutathione allowed in same bag; follow clinic mixing order and aseptic technique.
Prime IV tubing with the prepared bag; remove air from line.
Establish IV access using aseptic technique; confirm patency with saline flush and secure with transparent dressing.
administration_steps: Start infusion of Bag 1 (250 ml Normal Saline with Vitamin C 2000 mg + Glutathione 1200 mg) using SLOW rate profile with minimum duration 60 minutes.
Set pump or drip rate to meet 250 ml over at least 60 minutes; adjust only within SLOW profile unless clinician directs otherwise.
Ask patient to report immediately: chest tightness, shortness of breath, dizziness, nausea, headache, flushing, itching/rash, or IV site pain/burning.
If mild discomfort occurs, slow the rate and reassess; if symptoms persist or worsen, pause infusion and follow escalation rules.

during_infusion_checks: Comfort check every 10–15 min (ask about nausea, dizziness, headache, palpitations/anxiety, chest symptoms).
IV site check every 10–15 min (pain/burning, swelling, redness, infiltration).
Recheck BP/HR/SpO2 as needed if symptomatic or if baseline BP is low-normal.
stop_rules: Stop immediately and call clinician if: chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting / near-fainting, rapidly worsening symptoms.
escalation_rules: Pause infusion and reassess if: moderate nausea, moderate dizziness, moderate headache, IV site pain/burning, or patient asks to stop.
If symptoms improve after pause/slow rate, resume at slower rate; if not improving, stop and call clinician.

post_care: At end of infusion, stop drip/pump and flush line per clinic protocol.
Record end-of-session vitals: BP, HR, SpO2.
Remove IV cannula if no further therapy planned; apply pressure and dressing; provide aftercare instructions for site care.
Ask patient about post-infusion symptoms (lightheadedness, nausea, headache, palpitations) and document; provide oral water and allow seated recovery before standing.
Advise patient to seek urgent care if they develop chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or rapidly worsening symptoms after leaving.
documentation: all additives and final doses actually administered
start time, end time, total duration
rate profile used and any rate changes
clinician_signoff_required_if: Any hard-stop symptom is present at baseline (chest pain now, shortness of breath now, fainting episode today, confusion or severe weakness now).
Any moderate or severe reaction occurs during infusion (worsening nausea/dizziness/headache, rash/itching, breathing symptoms, near-syncope).
Any key safety item is Yes/Unsure or unclear (pregnancy/breastfeeding, kidney disease, G6PD deficiency, severe allergy/anaphylaxis, asthma/reactive airway, seizures).
Any significant abnormal vital sign trend occurs during infusion (symptomatic hypotension, new tachycardia, or SpO2 drop).
